parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hey, Nina, have you chosen a selective course yet?

Not really, Rick. I haven’t made up my mind yet. What about you?

Me either. We have to decide as soon as possible, though.

Why? Today’s not the final day for choosing selective courses, is it?

No, but they’ll be booked up very soon. Actually, some courses are already full.

Really? That’s too bad. Well, I was thinking of taking a language course. What do you think?

Yes, you can do that. You can choose all courses on the school website except mathematics, since it’s a required course for all students. By the way, I think business course is a good choice.

Yeah, it’s not bad. I think it’s going to be quite helpful after we graduate.

I think so. Guess what? I wanted to choose information statistics.

Why?

It’s related to our major, so I think it’s very useful for us. I mean, we will have an advantage in job hunting, but the bad thing is it’s in the morning, so we have to skip other classes in order to take it.

That’s not good. We need to find an alternative that is more convenient for us.

I know. It’s a shame. Nina, I think we need to get to know the courses more before choosing them. Otherwise, we may end up studying something that’s either boring or useless.

You’re right. Maybe we can look online to see if there’s information about it. We could also ask our parents for advice.

I don’t think that’s going to help much. People have all kinds of opinions online. We wouldn’t know which one to listen to. And our parents probably don’t know much about our field. I think the best way is asking the former students who have taken the class themselves. They can tell us how they thought about it from their own experience.

Oh, yes. They know it better than anyone.

Just like how much we know the art design class.

Yes. Before we took it last year, many people set on the internet that it was quite confusing, but it turned out to be quite easy and helpful, right?

It didn’t let us down. I definitely value the course. Design is an important skill in today’s world. Well, whatever course we want to choose, there are still things I need to figure out.

What do you mean? Do you mean things like the time of the courses?

Since it’s the first time we can choose selective courses, I need to know how to register. I think there will be instruction on our school website for registration. I’ll let you know.

You are so considerate, Nina. I think that’s necessary. We need to make sure we can register as soon as we make up our mind.

The courses we studied last semester were quite interesting. Maybe we could get some inspiration from those courses. Do you think so?

Well, yeah. Some of them were quite fun for me, such as metallurgy, though there were quite a lot of terms to remember.

But there’s also a lot of useful information about it on the internet, which made things easier.

That’s right. I can refer to many things when I was working on the paper.

And the professor in fluid mechanics was really patient. His explanation was crystal clear, so students had no difficulty understanding it.

Yes, that’s true. I was good at this course. What do you think of computing?

I think I was kind of boring in the beginning. Do you think so?

That’s exactly how I felt. There are a lot of numbers to deal with. But thankfully, it got more interesting when the course went on.

Right. Because later we could relate the theories to real life examples.

Exactly. Another course that I think was really practical is energy economy.

Oh, yes. There are a lot of practical works in the course. What we learned can come in handy in our future jobs.

We should make the decision based on our own experience and preference.

Yeah. Anyway, we really need to hurry up.

I’m sure we can reach a conclusion today.

questions.question: Why should they choose selective course immediately?

analyses.content: Rick 警告说虽然今天不是截止日，但课程很快就会被订满（booked up），甚至有些已经满了。
No, but they'll be booked up very soon. Actually, some courses are already full.
不要听到 "final day" 就选 A，原文明确否定了这一点（Today's not the final day）。

questions.question: What is the compulsory course for all students?

analyses.content: You can choose all courses on the school website except mathematics, since it's a required course for all students.
题目问的是 "compulsory"（必修），对应原文的 "required"，不要选 Language 或 Business，那是他们正在考虑的选修课。
Rick 指出除了数学（mathematics）以外的所有课程都可以选，因为数学是所有学生的必修课（required course）。

Rick 认为信息统计学与专业相关，对未来的求职非常有优势，即非常有用（useful）。

analyses.content: But there's also a lot of useful information about it on the internet, which made things easier.
虽然 Nina 提到了术语多（terms to remember），但两人最终共识在于网上资料带来的帮助。
关于冶金学（Metallurgy），Rick 指出互联网上有很多有用的信息（useful information... on the internet），让学习变得更容易。
And the professor in fluid mechanics was really patient. His explanation was crystal clear, so students had no difficulty understanding it.
"Crystal clear" 是一个固定搭配，形容像水晶一样透明清晰，直接对应选项 D（explanation was clear）。
关于流体力学（Fluid mechanics），Rick 称赞教授非常有耐心，解释得非常清楚（crystal clear）。
I think it was kind of boring in the beginning... But thankfully, it got more interesting when the course went on.
选项 A 的 "engaging" 是 "interesting" 的同义替换，不要因为听到 "boring in the beginning" 就忽略了后面的转折。
关于计算机（Computing），Nina 说刚开始很无聊，但随着课程进行，它变得越来越有趣（got more interesting）。
Oh, yes. There are a lot of practical works in the course.
听到 "practical works" 直接对应选项 C（involved lot of practical work），此处没有复杂的干扰。
关于能源经济（Energy economy），Nina 认为它很实用，Rick 补充说课程里有很多实际操作的工作（practical works）。
